name: Pantanal Conservation Area
blurb: A flooded plain where jaguars hunt caimans, capybara and fish.

tip.title: Hold back the flood
tip.text: The yearly flood spreads water, fish and nutrients across the plain. Turn Seasonal flood down and watch the aquatic plants, fish and then the predators that rely on them.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Pantanal, Jaguar, Yacare caiman). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.name: Water hyacinth & floating plants
nodes.desc: Floating and rooted aquatic plants that carpet the ponds and channels of the floodplain and feed grazers and snails.
Grasses of the seasonally flooded meadows. Capybara graze them, and when floodwater covers them they die back and rot in the water.
A semi-aquatic grazer of grasses and water plants, living beside rivers and ponds. Jaguars, caimans and anacondas all prey on it.
A large deer of wet grassland and marshes. Jaguars take it when it is available.
An omnivore of forest and scrub that eats palm nuts and fruit. Jaguars prey on it.
A predatory fish of lagoons and rivers. It is eaten by giant otters and jaguars.
Family groups hunt fish, especially piranha and catfish. The Pantanal is a key habitat and its numbers have recovered there.
Eats snails and fish, and occasionally capybara. About 10 million live in the Pantanal after a ban on the skin trade.
Soaring scavenger that cleans up carcasses, including capybara, across the wetland.
Top predator. In the Pantanal it feeds on aquatic reptiles and fish, and also on capybara, deer and peccary, often hunting in the water.
Year-round warmth and light let floodplain plants grow fast when water is present.
Most rain falls from November to March and feeds the rivers that flood the plain.
Around 80 percent of the floodplain goes under water in the wet season, moving fish, nutrients and plant matter across the wetland.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Rot the plants and animals that die in the water and soil and return nutrients, using up oxygen in the process.

story: The Pantanal is the world's largest tropical wetland and flooded grassland. About 80% of its floodplains go under water in the rainy season. It holds one of the largest jaguar populations on Earth, plus capybara and yacare caiman. A 1996 count put caimans at 10 million.
matters: It shelters migratory birds, nursery grounds for aquatic life, and refuges for yacare caiman, deer and jaguars. It has 463 bird species and 269 fish species.
